record_notes.DCP-LETT-2037F: January 8, supplied 1857; all three blocks, three notes and bibliography read. Complete short two-page ALS despite F suffix, not a fragment merely from ID. Thanks missing note and asks Doubleday to wait until well, but P3 explicitly clarifies interest in forms reared from a brood that others named separate species. That concrete question supplies a supported later response even though initial salutation section is mainly thanks. Historical request to defer work is source content, not a block on research.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2044: January 26, 1857 damaged four-page ALS; all ten blocks, six notes, separate annotations and bibliography read. Specimens sent with letter, not yet proven Darwin received. P2–4 three numbered specimen groups, plus-mark links one to Linnaean specimen; do not confuse field list with letter dates. Reared larval broods and Harpalyce single-female experiments distinguish true species from named variants, while adult similarity of Acronycta conceals larval differences. Typical female versus yellow-banded female experiments produce different distributions of offspring; not every form in every brood. Scottish darker shades and environmental observations qualified. No box return desired. Undated chapter/first-letter annotations separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2032: Before February 5, 1857 incomplete ALS; all four surviving blocks and three notes read, no bibliography section. Starts mid-question about all varieties from same eggs; identity supported by January 26 source and February 5 answer. Received box and read cover, relieving mistaken worry about return packing because sender said no return. Peronea colour and size query survives. Beginning missing, so February 5 reply local-variation question cannot be reconstructed into prompt. Relational composition range January 26 through February 4, inclusive earliest possible day only; no exact day or delivery date asserted.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-2047: February 5, 1857; all nine blocks, seven notes, full separate Darwin annotations/note and bibliography read. Thanks for acceptance of specimens, future further material conditional. Expands nominal-species correction and distinguishes Harpalyce immanata from russata, yellow band only latter. P5 explicitly answers local-variation query from missing part of Darwin letter; attribution via Logan retained. Seasonal brood differences include opposite size pattern in Pieris. P8 rearing from similar larvae and indiscriminate mating supports conspecificity but is not proof all forms were from a single clutch; two females confined on sallow are a separate example. Raw Peristera wording and unknown larva retained without silently substituting cristana. List promised in P8 is preserved in archive per apparatus but not transcribed on web page. Packing response matches Darwin P3. Separate Darwin note expressly February 8, 1857 supports known-by bound, not exact receipt; other marks undated and note is not Doubleday voice.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
